security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation false positives from markdown backticks, localhost URLs, and placeholder GEMINI_API_KEY usage. Confirmed issues are persistent shell-profile secret storage, curl-to-shell installation advice, and a FastAPI example that binds to all interfaces.

remediation.issue: The troubleshooting guide recommends curl piped directly to sh for uv installation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with package-manager instructions, checksum verification, or a link to official installation steps users can review first.
Recommend a per-session export, a local ignored secrets file, or a managed secret store instead of editing a shell profile.

remediation.issue: The FastAPI sample binds uvicorn to 0.0.0.0.
remediation.suggestion: Default local examples to 127.0.0.1 and explain when all-interface binding is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Python developers need reliable Genkit guidance because the SDK changes quickly. This skill provides current patterns for setup, flows, tools, Dotprompt, FastAPI, evals, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains Genkit Python setup with uv, virtual environments, plugins, and provider configuration.
Provides examples for generation, structured output, streaming, flows, tools, and embeddings.
Guides FastAPI integration with Genkit handlers, SSE streaming, and route decorator order.
Documents Dotprompt files, prompt variants, helpers, partials, and rendering for evals.
Covers Genkit evaluators, datasets, CLI eval runs, and common SDK error fixes.
limitations: Requires a working Python environment and a provider API key supplied by the developer.
Examples mainly assume Google AI and must be adapted for other providers.
Cannot verify live SDK changes unless the agent checks upstream documentation.
Does not deploy infrastructure or secure production endpoints automatically.

use_cases.title: Start a Genkit Python Project
use_cases.description: Create a new project with uv, install Genkit packages, configure a provider, and run the Dev UI.

use_cases.title: Serve AI Flows with FastAPI
use_cases.description: Expose Genkit flows through FastAPI routes, stream responses, and test local endpoints.

use_cases.title: Improve AI App Quality
use_cases.description: Organize prompts, add evaluators, use structured outputs, and diagnose common Genkit errors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter App
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Genkit Python starter app with Google AI. Include setup steps, flow structure, and Dev UI testing instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a Pydantic-backed tool to my Genkit flow. Explain the schema, decorator, and common Gemini parameter errors.

prompt_templates.title: Serve a Streaming Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a streaming FastAPI endpoint for this Genkit flow. Include decorator order, chunk behavior, and local verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Genkit Python project for API mismatches, prompt organization, eval coverage, and production readiness. Prioritize actionable fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a new Genkit Python project for a summarizer.

A flow outline and Dev UI run checklist.

output_examples.input: Expose a streaming chat flow through FastAPI.
output: Decorator order for the route and flow.
SSE client behavior in plain language.
Local test steps for the Genkit Dev UI.

output_examples.input: Debug a Genkit import or model error.
output: Likely cause, correction, and reference file to check.
A concise next action for the developer.
Warnings about outdated internal APIs when relevant.

best_practices: Verify imports and API names against the included references or upstream documentation.
Keep API keys out of source control, shell profiles, screenshots, and shared logs.
Test flows in the Dev UI before adding FastAPI serving or eval automation.
anti_patterns: Using internal Genkit modules instead of public package paths.
Defining tool parameters as bare scalar values instead of Pydantic models.
Binding local development servers to all interfaces without a clear need.

faq.question: Does this skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives commands for the developer to review and run in their own environment.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support FastAPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Genkit FastAPI handler guidance, streaming examples, and local endpoint testing steps.

faq.question: Can it help with Dotprompt?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains prompt files, schemas, variants, helpers, partials, and rendering.

faq.question: Does it cover evaluation workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes datasets, built-in evaluators, custom evaluators, and CLI eval runs.

faq.question: Is it provider specific?
faq.answer: Most examples use Google AI, but the same patterns can be adapted for other Genkit plugins.
